clue.text: Silver-plated souvenir at home is deteriorating

indicators.note: plated means coated all round, so the silver letters wrap around the rest

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a trophy is a souvenir kept from a win or a hunt
at home means in

explanation.surface: Someone's silver-plated keepsake is tarnishing at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver-plated' reads as one adjective describing the souvenir, but 'plated' is the container signal working on silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasting away and declining in strength are the same process, a synonym.

clue.text: Attempt to carry article — get this?

definitions.text: Attempt to carry article — get this?

indicators.note: to carry means the first word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: an attempt is a try
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A challenge to bear an object, with a teasing question to the solver.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes the answer: a flat board on which articles are carried.
explanation.definitionFit: A tray is the flat board waiters use to carry things, which is what the whole clue pictures.

clue.text: Where clothes may be available through computer network

definitions.meaning: washing hangs on a clothes line, and goods can also be bought over the internet
connected via or by means of the internet

explanation.surface: Where garments can be bought by way of a computer network.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing pegged out hangs on a line, and internet shopping happens via the web, two senses.

clue.text: Difficult to get hold of answer in formal record

indicators.note: to get hold of means the first word grips the next piece inside it

parts.note: difficult means hard

explanation.surface: A tricky thing to locate a reply in the official minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: HANSARD is the published official record of debates in the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed transcript of parliamentary proceedings is an official, formal record of what was said.

clue.text: Fence has this metal at front

definitions.text: Fence has this metal at front

parts.words: Fence has this metal at front
parts.note: the word fence begins with Fe, the chemical symbol of a particular metal

explanation.surface: A railing with a metal cap on its front.
explanation.walkthrough: You think of a metal railing, but the clue is about the word itself: FENCE starts with FE, the symbol for this element.
explanation.definitionFit: Fe is the chemical symbol of this element, and those letters open the word fence.

clue.text: Retire as head of government having got booted out

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of government
out signals that the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prime minister retiring after being kicked out of office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retire' looks like stepping down from office, but means turning in for the night. 'out' rearranges the word booted, giving OTOBED; 'having got' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: To retire for the night is an idiom for heading off to sleep.

clue.text: Pair come to dance when firm's laid on entertainment

indicators.note: in a down answer, laid on means placed on top, so the company letters come first

parts.note: a firm is a company, abbreviated CO; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: to dance means the letters jig about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple turn up to dance once the company has provided a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to dance' shuffles PAIR COME into MICOPERA; 'laid on' puts CO (firm) above it in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A light, humorous opera with a happy ending is a kind of stage show, an example.

clue.text: Imitation diamond gives shrine false quality

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
tone is a quality, as of a voice or colour

explanation.surface: A fake gem lends a holy place a counterfeit character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false' shuffles the word shrine into RHINES; 'gives' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhinestone is a paste gem made of glass cut to look like a real jewel.

clue.text: Henry and Thomas brought back insect

indicators.note: brought back means the combined letters are read from right to left

parts.note: H is the symbol for henry, the unit of inductance
Tom is short for Thomas

explanation.surface: Two men named Henry and Thomas returned with a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: H (henry) followed by TOM, then 'brought back' turns the whole run around.
explanation.definitionFit: A night-flying winged creature related to butterflies, an example of an insect.

clue.text: Disagreeing there's a decrease in disease

parts.note: a fall is a decrease
gout is a disease that inflames the joints

explanation.surface: Someone argues that cases of an illness are dropping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there's a' is link; the pieces simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarrel between friends is a falling-out, so the phrase means arguing.

clue.text: Work not about — one's restricted choice

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: restricted means held in, so the one letter is enclosed
about means the word not is turned round

parts.note: taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A job without fuss leaves someone with limited choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the word not into TON; 'restricted' shuts the one letter inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An alternative you may pick is a choice, a synonym.

clue.text: What could be nastier? It gets you crying

indicators.note: what could be means another arrangement of the following word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about what could be worse, answered by someone weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What could be' rearranges NASTIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Being reduced to weeping is an idiom for openly shedding drops from the eyes.

clue.text: I will repeat: 'I cannot read'

parts.note: I'll is the contraction of I will
to iterate is to repeat

explanation.surface: Someone says again that they are unable to read.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the claim such a person makes about themself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to read words is unlettered, so the quote is their own description.

clue.text: Criticise someone's perspective, then add question

parts.note: a person's take on something is their view of it
to tot up is to add
to question is to ask

explanation.surface: Criticise a person's viewpoint and then pose a question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'then' is link. TOT means add, as in totting up a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprimand somebody sharply is an idiom for finding fault with them.

clue.text: Swamped by dross, a veritable hoarder

indicators.note: swamped by means the letters lie buried within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps everything, buried under true rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of dross, all of a, and the start of veritable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts things aside rather than spending them stores them, a synonym.

clue.text: The man in love, American seen as odious

parts.note: the man is he
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A man in love with an American is seen as hateful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen as' is link. O for love comes from the tennis score of nil.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked and abominable describe the same shockingly evil quality, a synonym.

clue.text: Passing problem made an impact on church

parts.note: to make an impact on is to hit

explanation.surface: A temporary snag struck a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' means temporary: a short-lived snag.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary difficulty or snag that holds things up is a synonym.

clue.text: Boy of six hugged by father

indicators.note: hugged by means the six letters are held inside the father word

parts.note: dad is father
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A six-year-old son embraced by his dad.
explanation.definitionFit: A common boy's name, so a male given name stands for a boy.

clue.text: Be fond of liberal president

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: Feeling affection for a politically liberal head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: To be fond of something is to enjoy it, a synonym.

clue.text: Note in some melody recalled

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A message held in a tune that is remembered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' marks the hidden letters and 'recalled' sends them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A short written message or reminder is a note.

clue.text: Respond in respect of insincere performance

parts.note: re means concerning or in respect of
an act is a show put on, not genuine

explanation.surface: Reply regarding someone's fake show of feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond to something is to answer it with a reaction, a synonym.

clue.text: I get errand organised to catch poultry finally?

definitions.text: I get errand organised to catch poultry finally?

indicators.note: to catch means the anagram holds the next letter inside it
organised means put into order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word poultry

explanation.surface: A speaker says they have arranged a chore so as to seize some chickens.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'I' is the fox of folklore, whose errand is catching hens. 'organised' turns ERRAND into RENARD and 'to catch' takes in Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The fox of medieval fables bears this name, and foxes raid henhouses for poultry.

clue.text: Number gathered round goddess in the capital

indicators.note: gathered round means the number word surrounds the goddess letters

parts.note: ten is a number
Hera is the Greek queen of the gods

explanation.surface: A group of ten clustered round a goddess in a city.
explanation.walkthrough: An older spelling of TEHRAN, capital of Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: The main city of Iran, the seat of its government, so an example of a capital.

clue.text: Surprisingly alert when entertaining that heartless gossip

indicators.note: entertaining means taking in as a guest, so one piece is placed within the other
surprisingly means the word alert turns up rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters of that are removed, leaving its first and last

explanation.surface: An unexpectedly watchful person gives hospitality to a cruel gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' rearranges the word alert to TALER, and 'heartless' empties the middle of that; 'when' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tells tales is a talebearer, a gossip, a synonym.

clue.text: In this place get hold of culinary plants

indicators.note: in means the grasping word goes inside the place word

parts.note: this place is here
to bag is to get hold of or catch

explanation.surface: An instruction to collect kitchen herbs from a particular spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like part of the phrase 'In this place', but it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbs as a group, including those used in cooking, are this collective noun.

clue.text: Composer with support at front of harpsichord to take manuscript

parts.note: a bra is a support garment

indicators.note: front of means the first letter of harpsichord

explanation.surface: A musician takes a score after propping up a harpsichord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with', 'at' and 'to take' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A German Romantic who wrote four symphonies, an example of a composer.

clue.text: Keep control having captured army

indicators.note: having captured means the control word encloses the army letters

parts.note: a rein is a control, as in rein in
TA is the Territorial Army, the UK's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Holding power after seizing the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold on to something is to keep it, a synonym.

clue.text: Couple carrying on? The thing that's upset me

parts.note: it is the thing

indicators.note: upset in a down light means turned upside down, so the word me is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pair having an affair, and what is upsetting me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying on' means having an affair; a couple seen together is said to be an item. 'upset' turns ME into EM.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantically linked pair is called an item, an idiom.

clue.text: Man and daughter falling off sofa

indicators.note: falling off means the daughter letter drops away

parts.note: a divan is a sofa or low couch

explanation.surface: A man and his daughter tumble off the settee.
explanation.definitionFit: A common Russian boy's name, so a male given name stands for a man.

clue.text: Last course — then have liquid that's undrinkable!

parts.note: afters is British slang for dessert, the final course
taken as written

explanation.surface: Finish the dessert, then have a drink you should not swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'then' is link. AFTERS is British informal for pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Scented lotion splashed on after a shave is a fluid not meant for drinking.

clue.text: Action of the flipping captain before match?

definitions.text: Action of the flipping captain before match?

parts.words: Action of the flipping captain before match?
parts.note: a team leader spins a coin into the air before kick-off; flipping also reads as a mild curse

explanation.definitionFit: Before a game, captains flip a coin to decide who starts or chooses ends.

clue.text: Turning into a devil? That could be me, doing sin

indicators.note: could be means these letters may form a different word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asking who becomes a fiend, the speaker admits their own sinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges ME DOING SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Portraying someone as wicked or becoming fiendish, a verb from the word for an evil spirit.
